newsitem.title: GERMANY: New file could delay judgment in Iran murder trial.
newsitem.headline: New file could delay judgment in Iran murder trial.

text.p: An extensive dossier compiled by the Iranian Foreign Ministry could delay the end of a Berlin murder trial which has damaged ties between Bonn and Tehran, state prosecutor Bruno Jost said on Thursday.
The file, which the Iranian Foreign Ministry gave to the German embassy in Tehran last week, contains information about a trial witness identified only as "Source C".
Jost told reporters at the Berlin courtroom where defence lawyers began their summing up on Thursday that the file was now being translated into German.
"We have to expect that the dossier could lead to a delay in the trial," he said.
The verdict in the murder trial, which has lasted more than three years, was originally expected in January.
An Iranian and four Lebanese are on trial for the murder of three Iranian dissidents and their translator in Berlin's "Mykonos" restaurant in September 1992.
Jost said in his summing up earlier this month that the shootings had been ordered by the Tehran leadership, prompting demonstrations at the German embassy in Tehran.
Protestors demanded his execution and called for all ties with Germany to be cut.
The German Foreign Ministry has said it wants to maintain relations with Iran and would keep cool over the threats. Germany is Iran's largest European trade partner.
Prosecutors said the 31-page document was a new attempt by Tehran to influence the outcome of the trial.
Prosecutor Wolfgang Wieland said it could be a "collection of false and doctored information, to undermine the witness".
The state prosecutors had partly based their accusations on information supplied by Source C.
The man, who fled Iran, testified under heavy security and his identity was kept secret for his own protection.

The first defence lawyer began summing up his case on Thursday. Both lawyers for the 29-year-old Lebanese Yussef Amin said he had acted as lookout during the attack and did not know the details of what was planned.
